articles.title: Limitcast 0.20.11: fixes a Windows failure when commands overlap
articles.excerpt: Limitcast 0.20.11 is available on npm. It fixes a Windows failure where two Limitcast commands running at the same time could exit with an error and lose a settings change. macOS and Linux are unchang…
articles.body: Limitcast 0.20.11 is available on npm. It fixes a Windows failure where two Limitcast commands running at the same time could exit with an error and lose a settings change. macOS and Linux are unchanged. All features remain free under the MIT License. Limitcast runs locally on macOS, Linux and Windows with Node.js 22 or later . The Claude Code, Codex and Grok plugins have also been updated to 0.20.11. What went wrong on Windows Limitcast saves its settings and state by writing a temporary file and then renaming it over the real one, so a hook that reads at the same moment never sees a half-written file. On Windows, that rename is refused with EPERM while another process has the destination file open.

articles.title: Stitch Photos on an Infinite Canvas With Magnetic Snapping (No Uploads)
articles.excerpt: Most “combine photos” tools are really templates: three slots, a fixed margin, a watermark, and an upload. That is fine for a quick social collage. It is a poor fit when you want a flush contact sheet…
articles.body: Most “combine photos” tools are really templates: three slots, a fixed margin, a watermark, and an upload. That is fine for a quick social collage. It is a poor fit when you want a flush contact sheet, a before/after strip with a 0 px seam, or a lookbook that is not a 2×2 square. The alternative is an infinite canvas in the browser: drop images, pan and zoom, snap edges together, crop without destroying the original pixels, and export PNG, JPG, or WEBP at 1×, 2×, or 3× — locally. Start with the layout job, not with decoration Write the output you need: A flush row of product shots A before/after pair with no gap A masonry-style mood board A comparison grid with even 16 px or 24 px gutters A freeform canvas you will later crop Those jobs want different snap behavior.

articles.excerpt: Lydia Hallie from the Claude Code team at Anthropic gave a talk called "Rethinking Claude Code Best Practices" (ai.engineer, about 17 minutes). Its premise: a year ago you corrected one session at a t…
articles.body: Lydia Hallie from the Claude Code team at Anthropic gave a talk called "Rethinking Claude Code Best Practices" (ai.engineer, about 17 minutes). Its premise: a year ago you corrected one session at a time, wrote emphatic reminders into CLAUDE.md , and either approved every command by hand or skipped permissions entirely. Now developers at Anthropic run dozens of sessions, and the advice has to change with it. She gives the scale inside Anthropic as about 2,500 changes a day in May and more than 30,000 a day in September. I run a small Kubernetes platform that I build with AI coding agents from three companies: Claude coordinates and verifies, OpenAI's Codex models and Google's Gemini models write code and review it.

articles.body: Why Add AI Voice to Your Discord Bot? Discord is already a hub for real‑time chat, gaming, and community building. Adding a voice component turns a text‑only bot into a more immersive experience—think automated announcements, dynamic NPC dialogue, or even a personal AI companion that can read messages out loud. With modern text‑to‑speech (TTS) services, you can generate natural‑sounding speech on the fly, and with voice‑cloning you can give your bot a unique personality that matches your brand or community vibe. In this article we’ll walk through how to plug a high‑quality TTS service into a Discord bot using Python. We’ll focus on ElevenLabs , a service that delivers ultra‑realistic speech and even lets you clone a voice with just a few minutes of audio.

articles.body: A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.

articles.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
articles.excerpt: The queen in the northern night sky is supposedly one of the easiest constellations to recognize — you just look for a W. Or is that an M?
articles.body: Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone.
